subject: GPU fleet rationing & customer queue — resolution plan
body:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Martinez <elena@orion-edge.com>
Date: Thu, 02 May 2028 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Orion Edge ramp request / potential allocation conflict (DEAL-8721)

Team — quick heads up. Orion (DEAL-8721) is asking to accelerate their reserved capacity ramp by moving 40 GPUs into Q3 instead of the originally agreed Q4 start.

Why this matters:
- Our current reserved pool projection shows a ~42 GPU shortfall during the proposed window once we factor in LumenCloud's Q3 tranche (already signed).
- If we fulfill Orion's request in full, Lumen faces a >30% delay on their committed ramp.

Immediate ask:
- Ops/infrastructure: can you confirm any short-term burst capacity (spot or partner) and ETA?
- Product/sales: recommend a prioritization approach we can present to both customers.

Attached: capacity_impact_matrix.xlsx (matrix with weeks, GPU inventory, and deal commitments).

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142

From: Elena Martinez <elena@orion-edge.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 May 2028 11:02:18 -0700
Subject: Re: Orion Edge ramp request / potential allocation conflict (DEAL-8721)

Ben / Marissa — appreciate the quick note. High level: our execs want the higher ramp because Q4 model release requires low-latency inference for 24/7 customer traffic. If we slip to Q4 it materially hurts go-live.

We can be flexible on billing terms (willing to accept a higher per-hour burst fee) but need some firm guarantees on minimum sustained throughput starting Aug 1.

Elena Martinez
VP Engineering, Orion Edge
elena@orion-edge.com

On Fri, 03 May 2028 09:40:05 -0700, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai> wrote:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 May 2028 09:40:05 -0700
Subject: RE: Orion Edge ramp request / potential allocation conflict (DEAL-8721)

Thanks for the details — reviewed the numbers and the attached matrix. TL;DR: we do not have the spare reserved GPUs to satisfy both Orion and Lumen at the full requested ramps in August. Options with rough ETA and trade-offs: 

1) Fast node procurement (3–4 weeks lead for additional rent-in nodes via our hyperscaler partners). Cost: high; risk: lead time and setup ops.
2) Soft-tranche reallocation: move 24 GPUs to Orion in Aug and hold remaining 16 as a balanced tranche for Lumen. This requires product approval for partial SLAs and a compensation clause.
3) Burst-to-spot fallback: allow Orion to burst to spot instances for non-critical traffic; provides capacity immediately but increases tail latency and may not pass their SLOs.
4) Contractual priority lane: temporarily elevate one customer to priority (preempt other customers' burst capacity) in exchange for higher fees and extended commitment.

Recommendation: approach #2 + #4 combined — give Orion a guaranteed 24-GPU tranche starting Aug 1 with a priority-burst clause that allows up to +16 GPUs when available, bill at premium for burst, and schedule procurement to close the gap by mid-Sept. This splits the delta and buys time.

I attached a short risk note in the matrix and marked the likely impact weeks. Ops notes: we can execute the tranche move with a 48–72 hour lead time once leadership approves.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Martinez <elena@orion-edge.com>
Date: Fri, 03 May 2028 14:10:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Orion Edge ramp request / potential allocation conflict (DEAL-8721)

Evelyn — looping you in for decision. Quick summary and proposed customer-facing compromise to present to Orion (copying Elena for transparency):

Summary:
- Lumen's signed commitment occupies the bulk of our current reserved capacity for early Aug.
- Orion requests an accelerated start; they are willing to accept premium billing for burst hours.

Customer-facing proposal (one-pager we can send today):
- Guarantee: 24 GPUs reserved from Aug 1 — Sep 30 (sustained throughput target to be written into SOW).
- Burst window: up to +16 GPUs when cluster utilization < 70% (billed at 1.8x rate).
- Procurement roadmap: we will add rent-in nodes to close the remaining 16-GPU gap by 2028-09-15; we will provide weekly capacity updates.
- Contract: sign revised SOW (DEAL-8721_SOW_v2.pdf) with priority-burst clause and an SLA carve-out for spot-backed bursts.

If approved, Ben will pitch the updated terms; Karthik/Ops to prepare a technical appendix and runbook.

Elena — does that split (24 guaranteed / up to +16 burst) get you to a workable go-live plan?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0199

Attachment: DEAL-8721_SOW_v2.pdf

On Sat, 04 May 2028 14:32:00 -0700, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai> wrote:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 04 May 2028 14:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Orion Edge ramp request / potential allocation conflict (DEAL-8721) — APPROVED (temp tranche)

Team — after weighing customer impact and retention risk, I approve the hybrid approach. Directions: 

1) Sales: offer Orion the 24-GPU guaranteed tranche starting Aug 1 and the burst terms Marissa outlined. Make premium pricing explicit and add a 12-month minimum commitment for the tranche.
2) Legal/Contracts: finalize the SOW addendum and include the SLA carve-out for spot-backed bursts; require signature within 7 business days.
3) Ops/Infra: prepare runbook for tranche migration (48–72h lead) and accelerate hyperscaler rent-in procurement with target completion 2028-09-15. Prioritize the procurement ticket in the vendor pipeline.
4) Finance: model the revenue uplift vs. margin delta for premium billing; provide a P&L note.

Ben — move forward with the customer conversation and get the signed SOW ASAP. Karthik/Priyom — prep the ops playbook and confirm the exact nodes we'll rent if approved.

I'll mark this as an approved temporary exception to the standard allocation policy; we will revisit at end of Q3.

Evelyn Hart
VP, Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference
evelyn_hart@redwood.ai | +1 650-555-0123
